existing_queue_api_control.protocol: Two fresh-process trials for each dataset/method at 1 and 8 workers. Alternate static list batch1d versus generator-backed dynamic queue batch1d_iter; same files, published 0.6.0 wheel, Poisson errors, 32 file tasks, 3 warm blocks. Both APIs reopen and decode every image. Every result is byte-identical to the same array oracle. Background-load screen applies to both APIs.

protocol: Apple M4 Pro, CPython 3.13.5, 1/2/4/8 workers, 2,000 2theta bins, solid-angle correction, polarization 0.965, Poisson errors. Supersampling n=15 for Pilatus1M and n=5 for Eiger9M; pixel-split has no subpixel count. Each batch has 32 file tasks: 32 separate TIFF copies of one Pilatus image, or 16 distinct real Eiger images read twice. All TIFFs are uncompressed signed int32. Every file-mode task freshly opens and decodes its file. pyFAI and azint receive the decoded int32 NumPy views and perform their own backend preprocessing; Dioptrin converts file pixels to float64 internally and its array control requires float64 arrays. These natural input dtypes differ from the earlier uniformly float64 integration-only comparison, so rates between those studies are not a controlled measure of file cost. The matched controls within this study provide that workflow comparison. Dioptrin uses the published 0.6.0 Python batch1d(path_list) API with num_workers=c and num_threads=1; it shares geometry/CSR tables and creates worker pools per batch. azint and pyFAI use persistent Python frame threads, one independent integrator state per worker; pyFAI keeps a separate initialized CSR engine per worker. All distribute equal contiguous file chunks, 32/c frames per worker. azint generic and CPU/LTO/fast-math are separate builds. OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 for pyFAI and c for azint matrix construction; no nested numerical-thread oversubscription. Calibration setup includes construction, the first file read/result and preparation of all engine states; lazy imports inside pyFAI.load remain included. File-worker creation is included each time in Dioptrin batch throughput. Two fresh-process trials per point, alternating variant order; three warm timing blocks targeting 0.5 s, including result allocation and release. Both file and array controls must satisfy <=3.6 other busy cores. File mode runs first, followed by the matched array control; only the later control retains the decoded image stack. File-pipeline RSS is sampled externally every 10 ms and excludes that later input stack. Live heap, USS and physical footprint are also retained. All trials inherit the host MallocNanoZone=0; MallocLargeCache is unset. File bytes are served through the normal macOS filesystem cache; caches are not flushed. Reported payload rates are logical file bytes, not measured physical-SSD bandwidth. The TIFF reader orientation is matched across libraries by a row flip, a correspondingly mirrored mask and an equivalent mirrored PONI geometry. The physical 2theta map was verified to within 3.4e-16 radians; pyFAI legacy solid-angle rounding differs by at most 1.4e-7 under the coordinate transformation. Every file/array output is checked against a one-worker array oracle for the same backend and coordinates. Algorithms and internal precision still differ between libraries. This is a local TIFF/Python workload, excluding acquisition, GUI processing and output-file writing.
stage_note: Worker-stage traces are separate diagnostic runs at eight workers. Dioptrin uses instrumented Rust 0.6.0 source equivalent to the native file-batch implementation, with outputs checked against the published wheel. Its read stage includes TIFF decoding, float64 conversion and row reversal. azint/pyFAI traces use the published Python interfaces; their read stage ends at the decoded NumPy view, so backend dtype/layout preprocessing remains in the integration stage. Stage percentages describe each implementation; they are not a subtraction of the two throughput measurements. Timed primary throughput always comes from the published Python interfaces.
